title: 84 Frederick women's shelter and Cambridge paramedic station
subtitle: Immigration profile received; King Street shelter closure, childcare and affordable housing debate over the Concession Road site.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee heard from delegates who described the lack of a dedicated shelter for women and gender-diverse people, then recommended that staff proceed with the proposed operating model for 84 Frederick Street {{vote:m5}}. The shelter would serve single women and gender-diverse and non-binary adults, with a maximum of 66 residents, apart from extreme weather protocols. Any change in who is served or how many must first be discussed with community partners, including Kitchener, and come back to Regional Council.

The committee also recommended that Regional Council support a paramedic services station at 651 Concession Road in Cambridge, the former Kinsmen Children's Centre, and approve debenture authority of $12,600,000 for a term up to 20 years {{vote:m7}}. A proposal to send the report back to staff to look at childcare and affordable housing on the site was defeated {{vote:m6}}.

The committee also received the 2024 Waterloo Region immigration profile for information. It asked staff to report back on how rising immigration affects community supports such as lunch programs and shelters. Council will consider the recommendations at a later meeting. The King Street shelter is due to close on March 31, 2025.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff proceed with the operating model for a shelter of up to 66 single women and gender-diverse and non-binary adults, with any change in population or size to be discussed with partners and reported to Council first {{vote:m5}}.
The committee defeated a motion to refer the Concession Road report back to staff to consider childcare and affordable housing before Council on August 28 {{vote:m6}}.

The committee recommended that Council support a Paramedic Services station on the former Kinsmen Children's Centre site and approve $12,600,000 in debenture authority over up to 20 years {{vote:m7}}.

debate: Delegates argued that co-ed shelters feel unsafe for many women and gender-diverse people, and that a dedicated shelter is needed. Several urged more shelter capacity and a gender-based analysis in the Region's data and planning.

One councillor asked whether the closed women's shelter's operator might have stayed had the Region offered the same funding as a partner instead of buying the building. Staff said the operator's board made an independent decision and that the Region responded to the gap.

Staff said the 84 Frederick shelter is not a one-for-one replacement for the King Street shelter, which closes March 31, 2025. Councillors asked that neighbours of King Street be kept informed. One councillor said a large shelter downtown is not the right long-term model and that shelters should be spread across the region.

On Concession Road, several councillors supported the paramedic station but wanted childcare or affordable housing considered. Staff said childcare raised safety and traffic concerns with ambulances, and that housing would require costly underground parking and was not affordable at this stage.

Supporters of moving ahead stressed slow ambulance response times in Cambridge and a delay of many months already. Paramedic leaders said the site was identified as an urgent need. A councillor from Cambridge raised a possible joint fire and paramedic station, and staff said they could speak with city staff.
